patterns.pattern: Access to features and data is controlled by user roles and permissions, with administrators or staff having elevated or unrestricted access.
patterns.example_phrasing: User actions and visibility are limited by assigned roles; admin/staff override most restrictions.

patterns.pattern: Each entity's data is isolated to its own account, preventing cross-account data access without explicit permissions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Data belonging to one account is not accessible from another unless permitted.

patterns.pattern: Booking, cancellation, and related actions may only occur within defined windows, often governed by configuration (‘scheduling window’, ‘cancellation cut-off’).
patterns.example_phrasing: Bookings and cancellations are limited to preset lead times and windows.

patterns.pattern: Parent-child entity relationships enforce cascading behaviors such as cascade delete or maintaining referential integrity.
patterns.example_phrasing: Deleting a parent entity automatically deletes or affects related child entities.

patterns.pattern: Resource or session capacity is limited, and attempts to overbook or exceed allowed numbers are prevented.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each resource or event cannot be booked beyond its capacity limit.

patterns.pattern: Some features, data, or extended limits are restricted to Pro or subscribed users.
patterns.example_phrasing: Advanced options or higher quotas are only available for Pro accounts.

patterns.pattern: Cancellation policies and requirements (such as mandatory reason input) depend on configuration or event type and are enforced by UI/API.
patterns.example_phrasing: Cancel actions may require user input (e.g. reason) based on event or system settings.

patterns.pattern: Authentication and authorization are required for all API access to enforce user security.
patterns.example_phrasing: APIs require users to have valid tokens and permissions.

patterns.pattern: Certain actions or content are in scope only if directly related to booking/scheduling; unrelated or policy-violating content is blocked.
patterns.example_phrasing: Actions outside the scheduling domain or violating policy are rejected.

patterns.pattern: Resource availability is governed by schedules; bookings are only possible within specified windows.
patterns.example_phrasing: Resources can be booked only in the periods defined by their schedule.

patterns.pattern: Bookings requiring confirmation or approval remain tentative until acted upon by an authorized user.
patterns.example_phrasing: Some bookings need explicit approval before being confirmed.

patterns.pattern: Immutable or auditable records (e.g., invoices, orders, attendance) cannot be altered except via voiding, replacement, or special test modes.
patterns.example_phrasing: Issued records are permanent unless formally voided; test data is managed separately.

patterns.pattern: Attendance and participation for events or sessions must be explicitly logged or tracked by assigned staff.
patterns.example_phrasing: Relevant users must record or confirm participant attendance at events.

patterns.pattern: Personal or sensitive data (especially minors, health, or clinical details) is accessible only to authorized users, often with greater restrictions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Sensitive details are only visible or editable by specifically permitted users.

patterns.pattern: Recurring and one-off bookings/appointments are both supported, with recurrence defined by user or external system (e.g., calendar syncs).
patterns.example_phrasing: Events may recur based on system or external calendar definitions.

patterns.pattern: Parent guardians must be able to manage bookings, consents, and information for minors under their account.
patterns.example_phrasing: Parents can enroll, submit consent, and view/manage info for their children.

patterns.pattern: User setup or onboarding flows are required to initialize or activate accounts.
patterns.example_phrasing: System guides first user through initial setup or account creation.

patterns.pattern: Linked accounts or providers may only be connected once per entity; duplicates are not allowed.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each provider (e.g., calendar) can only be linked to one account at a time.

patterns.pattern: Overlapping bookings or schedule conflicts are prohibited within a cohort, class, or resource.
patterns.example_phrasing: Sessions in the same group must not overlap in time.

patterns.pattern: Automatic cleanup or expiry (e.g., of polls or test data) happens after inactivity or based on user type.
patterns.example_phrasing: Data is auto-deleted after a grace period, unless the user has special status.
